outputs.notes: AlertSourceFeature extended in features/alerts/types.ts with two new values: 'gradebook' and 'compliance' (Alert shape unchanged). getAlerts() in features/alerts/server/service.ts now emits three new alert kinds in addition to the UNCHANGED existing planner (pending_lessons) and attendance (attendance_missing) alerts — both of those were left exactly as-is and their tests still pass. New emitters: (1) GRADEBOOK — reads listGradebookSummaries(householdId) [from @/features/gradebook/server/repository], added to the top-level Promise.all; emits one alert per subjectId in a target learner's summary.needsAttentionSubjects (type 'gradebook_needs_attention', severity 'medium', sourceFeature 'gradebook', childId=learnerId, href '/growth/gradebook?childId=<learnerId>'); respects the childId filter via targetChildIds set. (2) COMPLIANCE — getActiveSchoolYear(householdId) [from @/features/school-year/server/service] fetched in the Promise.all; when present AND when no childId filter is active (household-scoped, mirrors the attendance household alert), awaits listDeadlines(householdId, schoolYear.id) [from @/features/compliance/server/repository] and emits one alert per not-completed deadline whose dueDate <= today+DUE_SOON window (type 'compliance_deadline', severity 'medium', sourceFeature 'compliance', childId=null, href '/compliance'). DUE-SOON WINDOW VALUE = 14 days (const COMPLIANCE_DUE_SOON_DAYS = 14 in service.ts); condition is `deadline.dueDate <= addDaysIso(today, 14)` so overdue not-completed deadlines are also surfaced, far-out ones are excluded. addDaysIso() does UTC yyyy-mm-dd calendar math. (3) SCHEDULE IMBALANCE — computed inside the existing per-child loop from the already-fetched lessons: counts lessons with dueDate===today grouped by subjectId, emits when any subject count >=2 (type 'schedule_imbalance', severity 'low', sourceFeature 'planner', childId=child.id, href '/lessons?childId=<id>'). IMPORTANT for future phases: getAlerts now depends on gradebook repo, school-year service, and compliance repo — any test that exercises the REAL service (jest.requireActual) must mock @/features/gradebook/server/repository (listGradebookSummaries), @/features/school-year/server/service (getActiveSchoolYear), and @/features/compliance/server/repository (listDeadlines), or it will hit getDb() and throw. Both alerts test files were updated with those mocks (defaults: [] / null / []).

overallMastery = average of non-null subject masteryAverage values, rounded to 1 decimal place: Math.round((sum/count) * 10) / 10. Confirmed null (never 0) when a learner has no scored subjects — computed by filtering subjectResults to masteryAverage !== null before averaging; when that filtered list is empty overallMastery is set to null rather than defaulting to 0. Added as GradebookSummary.overallMastery?: number | null (optional) in features/gradebook/types.ts rather than required, specifically so out-of-scope fixture/test files (features/gradebook/__tests__/fixtures/mockGradebook.ts, features/alerts/__tests__/unit/alertRules.test.ts) that construct GradebookSummary object literals without the new field did not need to be touched — they remain valid under the optional field and were left untouched, staying strictly inside P3's fileScope. Computed in listGradebookSummaries in features/gradebook/server/repository.ts, reusing the already-computed per-subject masteryAverage (no extra DB query). Test file features/gradebook/__tests__/server/overallMastery.test.ts is a repository-level unit test that mocks getDb() directly (precedent: features/auth/__tests__/unit/passwordResetTokens.test.ts) rather than mocking at the repository boundary, since this test targets the repository function itself; it queues the 5 sequential Promise.all select() result sets (learners, subjects, scores, gradingScales, aggregationRules) and asserts overallMastery for: (1) two scored subjects averaging to 80, (2) a learner with zero scored subjects → null, (3) a learner with one scored (80) and one unscored (null) subject → 80, confirming the null subject is excluded rather than pulling the average down.

outputs.notes: ComplianceStatusCard is a self-fetching card (pattern: SchoolYearProgressCard) with no props and no context dependency, mounted directly in Zone C by a later phase. On mount it calls complianceApi.getActiveSchoolYearId(); when it resolves null (no active school year) the card renders the EMPTY STATE with heading text exactly "Set up compliance" plus one line of body copy ("Configure a school year to track your homeschool compliance status.") and does NOT call getStatus/getDeadlines. When an id resolves, it calls complianceApi.getStatus('', schoolYearId) and complianceApi.getDeadlines('', schoolYearId) in parallel (householdId arg is unused by the API client, matching complianceApi's existing _householdId-ignored signature) and renders: status icon/label (green="On track", yellow="Needs attention", red="Action required", same color/label convention as CompliancePage.tsx StatusHero) plus all of StatusEngineResult.reasons, and a "Next deadline" section. NEXT DEADLINE SELECTION: filter deadlines to isCompleted === false, then sort by dueDate ascending (string compare on ISO yyyy-mm-dd) and take the first -- i.e. the earliest not-completed deadline; completed deadlines are always excluded even if their dueDate is earlier. When no pending deadlines exist the section reads "No upcoming deadlines". Loading state renders a data-testid="compliance-status-card-loading" skeleton (animate-pulse bars, same shape as PersonalTodoList/SchoolYearProgressCard skeletons); fetch error (any rejected promise in the getActiveSchoolYearId chain) renders data-testid="compliance-status-card-error" with copy "Couldn't load compliance status." and a Retry button that re-invokes the same load() function. Populated state root has data-testid="compliance-status-card". P7 (dashboard re-shell) should import { ComplianceStatusCard } from "@/features/dashboard/front/components/ComplianceStatusCard" and mount it directly in Zone C with no props.

DEFERRED per the plan's own explicit hedge ('If zero client aggregation is preferred, skip this phase and open a follow-up for a learning-time weekly-summary endpoint'). No LearningTimeWeekCard.tsx or its test were created — nothing built inside fileScope. Rationale: (1) learningTimeApi.list(filters) (features/learning-time/front/services/api.ts) only accepts a single optional learnerId plus from/to — there is no household-wide session list. A household-scoped weekly card would need one fetch per active learner (mirroring the N-per-child fan-out LearnerCommandCenter already does in P5: 1 + 2N fetches) just to bucket sessions into weekday bars client-side, which is materially more than the 'cheap' tier this phase was routed at. (2) Zone C is already dense after P7 (ComplianceStatusCard, SchoolYearProgressCard, QuranStreak rings, IslamicCalendarCard countdowns, full-width PersonalTodoList) — adding another self-fetching card competes for the same real estate P7 just slimmed down, and doing it well (per-learner or household-aggregated bars) is a genuine design decision, not a mechanical one. FOLLOW-UP: open a ticket for a GET /api/learning-time/summary?householdId=&from=&to= (or similar) endpoint that returns server-aggregated weekday totals across all active learners in one call, then build LearningTimeWeekCard.tsx as a thin renderer over that endpoint (no client bucketing) — this avoids the N-per-child fetch fan-out and matches the 'cheap' tier this phase was originally routed at. No files changed; progress.json is the only change for this phase.
